correctness.rationale: The record/occupation indicators were reconstructed from strict records relative to S0=0 and occupation of S1,S2,S3>0. Symmetric atomless signs are iid fair, independent of magnitudes. Independent sign-case reasoning yields all nine mixed moments, with only I1 J3 depending on t=P(B1>B2+B3); the special I3 J2 cell is integral_1/2^1 u/2 du+integral_0^1/2 u^2 du =11/48. Their sum is 35/12-t/8; ER3=19/16 and EA3=3/2, yielding covariance 109/96-t/8. Three exchangeable disjoint dominance events imply 0<=t<=1/3; a common narrow positive magnitude interval has positive probability, giving t<1/3 for every atomless law. Magnitudes supported on (1,1.5) achieve t=0; widely separated continuous scale mixtures approach t=1/3; mixing yields every intermediate t continuously. Horizons 1 and 2 are directly computable. An independent fresh 600000-path MC each for uniform and Gaussian jumps corroborated benchmark covariance within sampling variation; it cannot prove the sharp continuum interval.

value.rationale: Record-count and positive-occupation are two classical natural random-walk observables whose separate laws are universal. Identifying exactly the first horizon where their dependence reflects the jump-magnitude distribution is a meaningful structural boundary. The explicit triangle-inequality parameter and complete attainable interval with sharp strict infimum characterize the full three-step family, rather than a single counterexample or handpicked numerical point.

final_claim: For symmetric atomless iid real random-walk increments the three-step strict-record/positive-partial-sum-occupation covariance is 109/96 - P(B1>B2+B3)/8 and its exact attainable range is (35/32,109/96], while horizons one and two have distribution-free covariance 1/4 and 5/8.
limitations: Exactly n=1,2,3 covariance, symmetric iid atomless increments; strict comparisons, no lattice ties.
Monte Carlo was independent finite corroboration only, not proof of distribution-free identities.
No all-horizon joint law or higher-order correlation classification.
